newsitem.title: GERMANY: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUG 13.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and
Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - German television broadcasters host TV stars and famous boxers and premier new programmes at the industry's first trade fair aimed at boosting sales of advertising space as market growth slows. (Reuters)
MUNICH - The sports rights-buying arm of Germany's Kirch Group, ISPR, says it has signed a worldwide exclusive marketing rights deal with international soccer goalkeeper Andreas Koepke. (Reuters)
FRANKFURT - The Commerzbank adopts a new marketing strategy by offering gifts to account holders who bring new customers to the bank. (Reuters)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Federal prosecutors search the offices of celebrity magazine Bunte and confiscate three alleged contracts between supermodel Claudia Schiffer and magician David Copperfield. The magazine had reported it had contracts signed by Schiffer and Copperfield stipulating that money would be exchanged for every time they met in public. (Reuters)

FRANKFURT - Cable television home shopping channel H.O.T. is now available to 365,000 households in the southwestern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg. In three weeks, another 180,000 cable customers in the state will be able to watch H.O.T., the station says. (Reuters)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - Thomy, the German unit of food company Nestle, has received a blackmail letter carrying a warning that its products have been poisoned, Frankfurt police say. Thomy, whose products include mustard and mayonnaise, has been targeted by blackmailers since August 1996. (Reuters)

BONN - Telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG dismisses as pure speculation a report that it and the Italian power group ENEL would make a bid for information technology group Olivetti. (Reuters)
FUERTH - Retail group Schickedanz could eventually increase its stake in Karstadt from the initial 20.3 percent as part of a strategic alliance, a Schickedanz spokesman says. (Reuters)
FRANKFURT - Chemical group Hoechst AG says it plans to set up a textile fibre plant with Multikarma Investama of Indonesia aimed at boosting Hoechst's European textile fibre business. (Reuters)
PEOPLE NEWS:
HAMBURG - Claus Jacobi is named editor-in-chief and publisher of the Welt am Sonntag newspaper, the Axel Springer Verlag says. (Reuters)
FRANKFURT - Karsten Roesel is new German sales director of Europcar. (Reuters)
WALLDORF - Mo Asumang is named host of private station ProSieben's erotic programme Liebe Suende. Her predecessor, Andrea Thilo, has moved to BBC1. (Kress)
Deborah Cole, Berlin Newsroom, 49-30-203-98114
